title: 29 Days: What the Man Does Between Appointments
excerpt: H&N built the in-person standard men didn't know they were missing. What they don't do is send you home with anything. The other 29 days are yours to own.
imageBrief: The Transition. A man in a well-worn but impeccably maintained dark suit — jacket draped over the arm of the chair beside him, tie loosened one pull. He is seated in a deep leather armchair, one shoe already off and on the floor, the second coming off now, his hands working the lace without looking down. A glass of bourbon sits on the side table to his right, untouched. Through the floor-to-ceiling window behind him, the city is blue-grey at dusk, the last light draining out of the sky. The interior light is amber and low — a single lamp, warm against the cool blue outside. He is not looking at the camera. He is looking at nothing in particular. The expression is not relief — it is the quiet accounting of a man who finished the day and knows what comes next. The emotional register is earned stillness: the moment between the work and the recovery, held by a man who treats both with equal seriousness.

title: The Standard Doesn't Stop at the Ankle: A Guide to Premium Foot Care for Men
excerpt: His face gets moisturizer. His shoes get cedar shoe trees. His suits get pressed. Somewhere around the ankle, the standard quietly stops — and nobody pointed it out until now. This is the room where that changes.

title: The Premium Foot Care Standard: What the Man in the Mirror Has Been Missing
excerpt: A man who maintains everything at a high standard has an Ankle Line — the invisible point where his practice stops. BSV exists to move that line. This is where it starts.
